clue.text: Cheer reverberated around international musical

indicators.note: around says the turned cheer wraps about the next piece
a sound that reverberates comes back, so the word for the cheer is read backwards

parts.note: rah is a shout of cheering, as in rah-rah

explanation.surface: Applause echoes round a theatre staging a global musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverberated' turns RAH into HAR, and 'around' puts I inside it. HAIR is the 1960s rock musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is the famous tribal rock musical of the late 1960s, so it is an example of the stage genre.

clue.text: Indian goddess supporting American League bases

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, so the goddess comes below the league

parts.note: AL is the abbreviation for baseball's American League
Kali is the Hindu goddess of time and destruction

explanation.surface: A Hindu deity backing a US baseball league, whose diamond has bases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' works only in a down entry, where the supporter sits underneath. 'bases' is the chemistry sense, not the baseball one the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an alkali is a soluble base, so alkalis are bases.

clue.text: Kubrick's initial sorry gripe about unknown one in 18

indicators.note: the initial of the director's name is its first letter
about says the rearranged gripe goes round the unknown
sorry in the sense of in a sorry state, so the word gripe is put into poor order

parts.note: Y is one of the letters used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Stanley Kubrick's first apology, with a moan about some unknown film crew member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorry' rearranges GRIPE to EGRIP; 'about' puts Y inside it after the E; K comes first. 18 is CREDITS: a key grip is listed in film credits.
explanation.definitionFit: A key grip is the chief stagehand on a film set, a job name listed among a movie's end titles.

clue.text: With difficulty carting no small amounts of treasure

indicators.note: carting means carrying, so the first piece holds the next one inside it

parts.note: something done with difficulty is done hard, as in hard-won
O stands for nought or no, as in a zero score
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Laboriously wheeling away caches of valuables, not small ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carting' puts O inside HARD to make HOARD, and S is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoards are hidden stores of valuables, stashes of coins or riches.

clue.text: Caught by a paramilitary organisation left bringing up the rear

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the UDA is the Ulster Defence Association, a loyalist paramilitary group in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone captured by a militia and abandoned at the back of the column.
explanation.walkthrough: The UDA (Ulster Defence Association) is a Northern Irish paramilitary group.
explanation.definitionFit: Caudal means relating to the tail, the part at the back of an animal.

clue.text: Tool for smoothing a piece of furniture

definitions.meaning: a tool that dresses stone or wood, trimming and finishing its surface
a kitchen sideboard with shelves above for plates

explanation.surface: A workshop implement for planing down a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress stone or timber is to finish its face, so the tool is named for that; separately, a Welsh dresser is a sideboard with shelving.

clue.text: This, in general, starts to bring on anticipated reduced drift

definitions.text: This, in general, starts to bring on anticipated reduced drift

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

indicators.note: starts to tells us to take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A sailor explaining a piece of gear that cuts sideways slip as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' hides the general himself, Robert E. Lee; 'starts to' takes opening letters. Read whole, the clue also describes what the device does.
explanation.definitionFit: A leeboard is a plank lowered over a sailing barge's side to stop it slipping sideways downwind.

clue.text: Understanding simple maths in the end

parts.note: light as in easy or undemanding, like light reading

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word maths

explanation.surface: Grasping basic arithmetic eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Understanding' is the sense in 'according to my lights', meaning by my own grasp of things.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lights are one's mental capacities or knowledge, as in 'by their lights', meaning to the best of their comprehension.

clue.text: Saleman's new lines hard to top up

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: new says the word lines is made afresh in another order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A salesperson's fresh spiel is tough to refill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the rearrangement signal. 'Saleman's' is printed without the second s of salesman's, a slip that does not affect the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish is to fill something again, restoring a supply that has run low.

clue.text: Organic green fare?

parts.note: produce reared outdoors without battery methods, which ethically minded shoppers buy; the letters of the last two words also rearrange into it

explanation.surface: Eco-friendly vegetables at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no anagram signal other than the question mark, so this reads as a cryptic definition with a bonus: green fare's letters spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Free-range food comes from animals allowed outdoors, which ethically minded buyers class with organic produce.

clue.text: Set of forwards

definitions.meaning: the objects dressing a stage or film set
rugby front-row players either side of the hooker

explanation.surface: A group of attacking players.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre props are the movable objects on stage, while in rugby the two props are front-row forwards.

clue.text: See 3
Scraps a piece of music, primarily syncopated

parts.note: a rag is a ragtime composition, like Scott Joplin's

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of the word syncopated

explanation.surface: A musician bins a jazzy tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraps' looks like a verb (discards) but is the noun: bits of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Rags are torn bits of cloth, leftover remnants.

clue.text: Is Mordred bitter about number in compound?

indicators.note: about says the first two pieces go round the number

parts.note: Mordred is the setter, so 'Is Mordred?' becomes the setter asking 'Am I?'
acid as in sharp and sour to taste

explanation.walkthrough: The setter's own name stands for 'I', so 'Is Mordred' is 'am I'; 'about' puts NO between AMI and ACID.
explanation.definitionFit: An amino acid is an organic molecule, one of the building blocks of proteins.

clue.text: Concerned to hold the editor's attention

parts.note: interest means curious attention, as in to hold someone's interest
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Anxious to keep the newspaper boss focused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold the' just links: the editor's attention is read as interest belonging to ED, put after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being interested in a matter means having a stake in it, as an interested party is involved.

clue.text: Note nester returning for part of a leaf

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: returning means the word for a nest builder is read backwards

parts.note: a bird is something that builds and sits in a nest

explanation.surface: A homing warbler leaves a note as part of its foliage nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' is the turnaround signal; 'nester' is a made-up word for something that nests.
explanation.definitionFit: The midrib is the central vein running down a leaf's length.

clue.text: Bob's yet to become one in 18

indicators.note: the letters are to become something else, a signal that they are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Bob still has ambitions to be a film technician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' rearranges BOBSYET. 18 is CREDITS: the best boy appears in a film's credits.
explanation.definitionFit: A best boy is the chief assistant to the gaffer or key grip on a film crew, a job listed on screen at the end.

clue.text: Somewhat suspect ingredient could be found in jam

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook suspects something dodgy in a jar of preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across suSPECT INgredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Pectin is the gelling agent from fruit that makes preserves set.

clue.text: Misguidedly directs balance sheet entries

indicators.note: misguidedly means in a wrong direction, so the letters of directs are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An accountant mistakenly instructs where figures go in the books.
explanation.definitionFit: In bookkeeping, credits are amounts recorded on the right-hand side of an account.

clue.text: Elevated Sachin Tendulkar primarily bats producing spectacular performances

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting the pieces up makes them read from bottom to top
primarily picks out the first letters of the cricketer's two names

parts.note: bats means crazy, as does nuts

explanation.surface: The great Indian batsman's raised bat yields dazzling shots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' turns STNUTS upwards into STUNTS. Sachin Tendulkar is India's great batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunts are daring feats done to impress, like acrobatic displays.

clue.text: One assembling material displaying sex appeal of Nora Batty's admirer getting nothing right

parts.note: Compo is the scruffy character in the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine who pined for Nora Batty; the 'of' makes it possessive, Compo's
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A typesetter shown with the allure of a sitcom suitor, coming to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex appeal of Nora Batty's admirer' is Compo's IT, read in that order. Last of the Summer Wine is a long-running British TV comedy set in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor is a typesetter, who arranges type for printing.

clue.text: Promote trendy piece of software

parts.note: to plug something is to advertise it
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Advertising a fashionable app.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug-in is an add-on module that extends a program's features.

clue.text: Intone liturgy enthralling leaders of ecumenical congregation

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the rite holds the leading letters inside

parts.note: a rite is a set form of worship

indicators.note: leaders of picks out the first letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: Chanting prayers that captivate an interdenominational church gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralling' is the container signal: the liturgy holds the leaders captive.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to speak aloud from memory, as a priest might chant prayers.

clue.text: Repeat part of speech on reflection

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a fragment taken from inside the following words

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a phrase in a talk is said again.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in speECH On. 'on reflection' is surface padding pointing at the sense: sound bounced back.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound repeated by reflection off a surface.

clue.text: Boy's beginning to quit cubs to supply him

definitions.text: Boy's beginning to quit cubs to supply him

indicators.note: to quit means the next piece leaves the pool of letters
read as supple-y, these letters are bent into a new order
the beginning of the word boy is its first letter

explanation.surface: A youth leader notes the young recruits who move up a section.
explanation.walkthrough: Take B (the beginning of Boy) out of CUBSTO and rearrange the rest; 'supply' is read as 'supplely', bending them. Cubs move up to become scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cub packs feed the Scout troop: older Cubs move up to become Scouts.

clue.text: Embracing popular culture initially in a large measure

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word culture

explanation.surface: Hugging pop culture heartily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C between A and LINCH, after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people in a clinch are holding each other tightly, hugging.

clue.text: Gang insufficient for railway junction

parts.note: Crewe in Cheshire is a famous English railway junction town

explanation.walkthrough: Crewe is an English town known as a major railway junction.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a group of people working together, a team or band.

clue.text: See 16
Those offering pupil advice plug eyeshades

parts.note: an ad promotes something, as a plug does
visors shade the eyes
